Every flag is a perfectly flat, front-facing rectangle with an aspect ratio of 41 to 26, all the same size, evenly spaced with identical black gutters; no perspective, no waving, no folds, no shadows, no frames, no poles, no swallowtails, no tassels, no fringes, no tabs, no finials, no pennant tails and no hanging ends: every flag is a plain rectangle, wider than it is tall, about 1.58 times as wide as it is tall. The look is a medieval embroidered silk banner: a deep, saturated silk field, one appliqued cloth device outlined with couched gold or silver thread, a restrained composition of one device with at most one small accent, and stylised heraldic drawing in the manner of medieval armorials and tapestries. A beast is a flat, elongated, posed heraldic silhouette in profile, with no fur strokes, no shading, no modelled musculature and no natural walking pose. A plain field is one unbroken tincture with no band, stripe or division of any kind, and no field is ever banded in three equal bands. No crenellated, toothed or stepped bar and no stepped or toothed line of division anywhere on the flag: every line of division is straight or simply curved. No castle walls, battlements, towers or gate-towers anywhere; any rayonny edge is drawn as soft, rounded rays, never as flame-shaped tongues. Each flag has one strong central device, stylised and heraldic, never naturalistic and never clip-art: no cartoon, no outline illustration, no pictorial scene, no landscape, no modern vector style, no fine detail smaller than one fortieth of the flag's height. Each flag's hand (how its devices are drawn), hem (its border ornament) and ground (its field pattern) are given in its style line and must be shown exactly. No lettering, no letters, numbers or runes anywhere; no signature or maker's mark; no real-world religious symbol; no real national flag or coat of arms; no crosses of any kind, no stars, crescents or eagles; no masonry or battlements. Family style: each people keeps its own line (see the people grammar). Family style: every line is nebuly, like a cord drawn through loops. Family style: every line is engrailed, and elven silver appears in every achievement. Shared palette of this sheet: holt green, root brown, pot gold, lake blue, deep grove, bark umber, moss pale, lamp gold, redbark, deep bark, antler bone, ochre, veil grey, char, undyed wool, kingdom green, old silver. Keyline: flags 2, 3, 4 have a near-black field; each of them is edged all round by a thin light-grey keyline (#a6a6a6), about two percent of the flag's width, drawn just inside the flag's own edge so it stands clear of the black ground. The keyline is the only addition; every tincture stays exactly as named.
Row 1, left to right: 1. A field divided across, holt green above and root brown below, by an escartelly line with one square notch. A gold torc, a plain neck-ring with open ends in pot gold, large in the centre. An orle (a narrow inner frame set in from the edges) of lake blue. The culture's hand: its devices built from one band woven over and under itself, like a knotted cord or a basket-work; its hem: a fringe of short tassels along the hem, in the second tincture; its ground: a ground counterchanged, its two tinctures swapped in a band across the middle of the field. 2. A field of deep grove with a base (a band across the bottom, two sevenths of the height) of bark umber edged by a rooted line from which short root-strands hang. An ancient tree with spreading roots in moss pale, large, standing on the base. A plain narrow border of lamp gold. The culture's hand: its devices segmented and jointed, like a carved totem, each part set one above another; its hem: a hem of twisted cord in the field's second tincture; its ground: a ground diapered with a small repeated motif in the second tincture. 3. A field divided upright, redbark at the hoist and deep bark at the fly, by a cloud-like interlocking line (nebuly), like a cord pulled through loops. A stag's antlers (attires) in antler bone, large in the centre. A beaded cord hanging in ochre, small, beneath it. The culture's hand: its devices built from one band woven over and under itself, like a knotted cord or a basket-work; its hem: a border of climbing vine-scroll, leaves and tendrils, in the second tincture; its ground: a ground strewn with a small motif in the second tincture, a dot or a bar, set in even rows.
Row 2, left to right: 4. A field divided across, veil grey above and char below, by a cloud-like interlocking line (nebuly), like a cord pulled through loops. A single loose knot in a cord, both ends hanging in undyed wool, large in the centre. The culture's hand: its devices segmented and jointed, like a carved totem, each part set one above another; its hem: a border of long pointed tags (dagging) along the lower edge; its ground: a plain ground of one tincture, without pattern. 5. A plain field of kingdom green. A single flame on a tall staff in old silver, large in the centre. The culture's hand: its devices ending in curling volutes and scrolls, like wrought iron or gilded scroll-work; its hem: a border of linked rings, like mail; its ground: a ground divided by a grid of small lozenges in the second tincture.

A flat asset image of ONE medieval banner cloth for a medieval-fantasy strategy game, on a canvas 1536 by 1024 pixels. The cloth of the flag fills the WHOLE canvas edge to edge: a flat front-facing textile with no background, no black ground, no border or frame outside the cloth, no pole, no fold, no waving, no shadow, no vignette, no glow and no gradient outside the cloth. Keep every device and every border at least six percent inside each edge of the canvas, so that nothing is cut at the top or bottom. The look is a medieval embroidered silk banner: a deep, saturated silk field, one appliqued cloth device outlined with couched gold or silver thread, a restrained composition of one device with at most one small accent, and stylised heraldic drawing. The cloth of the flag fills the WHOLE canvas edge to edge: a flat front-facing textile with no background, no black ground, no border or frame outside the cloth, no pole, no fold, no waving, no shadow, no vignette, no glow and no gradient outside the cloth. The look is a medieval embroidered silk banner: a deep, saturated silk field, one appliqued cloth device outlined with couched gold or silver thread, a restrained composition of one device with at most one small accent, and stylised heraldic drawing.
